name: RCW World Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a fully dated chain of 17 reigns from K.C. Colossus's tournament win on 8 November 1997 through Rob Holiday's tournament win on 21 October 2001 -- both tournament finals billed on the page itself for the "World/North American Championship," a compound name used only at those two bracket notes and nowhere else in the lineage, distinct from the fed's own separately-defended RCW North American Championship. The Executive holds the belt four separate times, K.C. Colossus three. The page's own ledger records the title vacant from 6 October to 21 October 2000, the last entry before that stretch carrying its own note "Federation closed," and then vacant again for a full year before Rob Holiday's own win -- an unexplained year-long gap in the source's own stated dates, recorded as it stands. The fed's own served Royal Rampage V recap (18 June 2000) corroborates one reign mid-chain, with The Executive successfully defending against Jack McGriff in a nine-fall main event.

name: RCW Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served Royal Rampage V recap catches this belt mid-lineage: "Sensational" Johnny Lee defends it in a Triple Threat Table Match against Kerry "Carnage" Carter and Raven Midknight on 18 June 2000, eliminated first by Carter, who is in turn eliminated by Midknight for the title. The surviving record opens with Lee already champion and gives no earlier reign.

name: RCW United States Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served Royal Rampage V recap catches Jake Rockwell as champion, successfully defending the belt against The Boog-man in a Crowbar-On-A-Pole Match on 18 June 2000. The surviving record neither dates his own win nor shows any further defense.

name: RCW North American Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served Royal Rampage V recap catches Adam Adonis as champion, retaining the belt over Nick Fury in a Ladder Match on 18 June 2000 by gouging Fury's eyes to grab it first. The surviving record neither dates his own win nor shows any further defense. A separate, distinct belt from the RCW World Championship, whose own tournament-win notes elsewhere in the held record use the compound name "World/North American Championship" for that title alone -- this belt's own concurrent, separately-defended existence at Royal Rampage V is the receipt that the two titles do not share one lineage.

name: RCW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served Royal Rampage V recap catches The Commission (Victor Shade & Donald Blake) as champions, retaining the belts over Strictly Business (Warren Knight & Jesse Bishop) by disqualification on 18 June 2000, when Dominion and Minions of Darkness ran in — the losing faction then threw the belts back down at the champions rather than raise them. The surviving record neither dates the champions' own win nor shows any further defense.
